children.name: Ammotragus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the aoudad or Barbary sheep, a large, shaggy-legged wild caprid native to North Africa's rocky mountains, now introduced and thriving in feral populations across the American Southwest and southern Europe.

children.name: Ammotragus lervia
children.description: The Barbary sheep (Ammotragus lervia), also known as aoudad (pronounced [ˈɑʊdæd]), is a species of caprine native to rocky mountains in North Africa and parts of West Africa.

children.name: Arabitragus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Arabian tahr, the smallest and most endangered tahr species, clinging to the rocky escarpments and cliffs of Oman's Hajar Mountains.

children.name: Arabitragus jayakari
children.description: The Arabian tahr (Arabitragus jayakari) is a species of tahr native to eastern Arabia.

children.name: Budorcas
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the takin, a massive, thick-set caprid of Himalayan and Chinese mountain forests with a unique moose-like face, thought by some to be the origin of the 'Golden Fleece' legend.

children.name: Budorcas bedfordi
children.description: Budorcas bedfordi (Golden Takin) is a takin species found in Asia region.

children.name: Budorcas taxicolor
children.description: The takin (Budorcas taxicolor);  is a large species of ungulate of the subfamily Caprinae found in the eastern Himalayas..

children.name: Budorcas tibetana
children.description: The Sichuan takin or Tibetan takin (Budorcas taxicolor tibetana) is a subspecies of takin (goat-antelope).

children.name: Budorcas whitei
children.description: Budorcas whitei (White's Takin) is a takin species found in Asia region.

children.name: Capra
children.description: The true wild goats and ibexes, around nine species of sure-footed mountain caprids distributed from Western Europe to the Himalayas, including the bezoar ibex ancestor of all domestic goats.

children.name: Capra aegagrus
children.description: The wild goat (Capra aegagrus) is a goat species, inhabiting forests, shrublands and rocky areas ranging from Turkey and the Caucasus in the west to Iran, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, and Pakistan in the east.

children.name: Capra caucasica
children.description: The West Caucasian tur (Capra caucasica) is a mountain-dwelling goat-antelope native to the western half of the Caucasus Mountains range, in Georgia and European Russia..

children.name: Capra cylindricornis
children.description: The East Caucasian tur (Capra cylindricornis) is a mountain-dwelling caprine living in the eastern half of the Greater Caucasus mountains, in Azerbaijan, Georgia, and European Russia..

children.name: Capra falconeri
children.description: The markhor (Capra falconeri)  is a large wild Capra species native to the mountain regions at the crossroads of Central and South Asia, including the Karakoram and Himalayas..

children.name: Capra hircus
children.description: The goat or domestic goat (Capra hircus) is a species of goat-antelope that is mostly kept as livestock..

children.name: Capra ibex
children.description: The Alpine ibex (Capra ibex), also known as the steinbock, is a European species of goat which lives in the Alps.

children.name: Capra nubiana
children.description: The Nubian ibex (Capra nubiana) is a desert-dwelling species of goat (genus Capra) found in mountainous areas of northern and northeast Africa, and the Middle East.

children.name: Capra pyrenaica
children.description: The Iberian ibex (Capra pyrenaica), also known as the Spanish ibex, Spanish wild goat and Iberian wild goat, is a species of ibex endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.

children.name: Capra sibirica
children.description: The Siberian ibex (Capra sibirica), also known using regionalized names including Altai ibex, Asian ibex, Central Asian ibex, Gobi ibex, Himalayan ibex, Mongolian ibex, and Tian Shan ibex, is a polytypic species of ibex, a wild relative of goats and sheep.

children.name: Capra walie
children.description: The Walia ibex (Capra walie, Amharic: ዋልያ wālyā) is a vulnerable species of ibex.

children.name: Capricornis
children.description: The serows, five species of goat-antelope found in rugged mountains and forests from the Himalayas to Japan and Southeast Asia, with a distinctive gland below each eye and coarse, shaggy coats.

children.name: Capricornis crispus
children.description: The (Capricornis crispus) (羚羊) is a Japanese goat-antelope, an even-toed ungulate.

children.name: Capricornis maritimus
children.description: Capricornis maritimus (Indochinese Serow) is a serow species found in Asia region.

children.name: Capricornis milneedwardsii
children.description: The mainland serow is a species of serow native to the Himalayas, Southeast Asia and China.

children.name: Capricornis rubidus
children.description: The red serow, also called the Burmese red serow, is a goat-antelope thought to be native to southern Bangladesh and northern Myanmar. It sometimes has been considered a subspecies of C. sumatraensis.

children.name: Capricornis sumatraensis
children.description: The mainland serow is a species of serow native to the Himalayas, Southeast Asia and China.

children.name: Capricornis swinhoei
children.description: The Taiwanese serow also known as the Formosan serow, is a small species of bovid that is endemic to Taiwan.

children.name: Capricornis thar
children.description: The Himalayan serow, also known as the thar, is a subspecies of the mainland serow native to the Himalayas. It was previously considered its own species, as Capricornis thar. It is the official state animal of the Indian state of Mizoram.

children.name: Hemitragus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Himalayan tahr, a large wild ungulate of the Himalayas with a dense reddish-brown mane and backward-curved horns, prized by hunters and widely introduced to New Zealand and South Africa.

children.name: Hemitragus jemlahicus
children.description: The Himalayan tahr is a large even-toed ungulate native to the Himalayas in southern Tibet, northern India, western Bhutan and Nepal. It is listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List, as the population is declining due to hunting and habitat loss.

children.name: Naemorhedus
children.description: The gorals, four small, nimble goat-antelopes of steep rocky terrain from the Himalayas to eastern Siberia and Korea, built for life on precipitous cliffs where few other mammals can follow.

children.name: Naemorhedus baileyi
children.description: The red goral is a species of even-toed ungulate in the subfamily Caprinae in the family Bovidae. It is found in India, China (Tibet) and Myanmar. Its natural habitats are seasonal mountainous areas 1,000 to 2,000 meters above sea level.

children.name: Naemorhedus bedfordi
children.description: Naemorhedus bedfordi (Bedford's Goral) is a goral species found in Asia region.

children.name: Naemorhedus caudatus
children.description: The long-tailed goral or Amur goral is a species of ungulate of the family Bovidae found in the mountains of eastern and northern Asia, including Russia, China, and Korea. A population of this species exists in the Korean Demilitarized Zone, near the tracks of the Donghae Bukbu Line. The species is classified as endangered in South Korea, with an estimated population less than 250.

children.name: Naemorhedus evansi
children.description: The Chinese goral (Naemorhedus griseus), also known as the grey long-tailed goral or central Chinese goral, is a species of goral, a small goat-like ungulate, native to mountainous regions of Myanmar, China, India, Thailand, Vietnam, and possibly Laos.

children.name: Naemorhedus goral
children.description: The Himalayan goral (Naemorhedus goral) or gray goral is a bovid species native to the Himalayas.

children.name: Naemorhedus griseus
children.description: The Chinese goral, also known as the grey long-tailed goral or central Chinese goral, is a species of goral, a small goat-like ungulate, native to mountainous regions of Myanmar, China, India, Thailand, Vietnam, and possibly Laos. In some parts of its range, it is overhunted. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has listed it as a "vulnerable species".

children.name: Nilgiritragus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Nilgiri tahr, an endangered wild ungulate endemic to the high shola grasslands and cliffs of India's Western Ghats, with males developing a pale saddle patch with age.

children.name: Nilgiritragus hylocrius
children.description: The Nilgiri tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius) is an ungulate that is endemic to the Nilgiri Hills and the southern portion of the Western Ghats in the Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

children.name: Oreamnos
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the mountain goat, North America's highest-altitude ungulate, whose thick white coat, cloven hooves with rough pads, and stocky frame allow it to navigate near-vertical cliffs in the Rocky Mountains.

children.name: Oreamnos americanus
children.description: The mountain goat (Oreamnos americanus), also known as the Rocky Mountain goat, is a cloven-footed mammal that is endemic to the remote and rugged mountainous areas of western North America.

children.name: Ovibos
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the musk ox, a shaggy Arctic ruminant that survived the Pleistocene extinctions, bearing the world's finest natural insulating fibre (qiviut) beneath its long outer guard hairs.

children.name: Ovibos moschatus
children.description: The muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae..

children.name: Ovis
children.description: The wild and domestic sheep, around seven species from the mouflon of Mediterranean islands to the argali of Central Asian high plateaux, including the ancestor of all domestic sheep breeds first domesticated c. 11,000 years ago.

children.name: Ovis ammon
children.description: ammon Category:Mammals of Central Asia Category:Mammals of Afghanistan Category:Mammals of China Category:Mammals of Pakistan.

children.name: Ovis arabica
children.description: Ovis arabica (Arabian Mouflon) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis aries
children.description: Category:Mammals described in 1758 Category:Animal taxa named by Carl Linnaeus.

children.name: Ovis bochariensis
children.description: Ovis bochariensis (Bukhara Urial) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis canadensis
children.description: The bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis) or bighorn is a species of sheep native to North America.

children.name: Ovis collium
children.description: Ovis collium (Kazakh Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis cycloceros
children.description: Ovis cycloceros (Afghan Urial) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis dalli
children.description: Dall sheep or thinhorn sheep (Ovis dalli), is a species of wild sheep native to northwestern North America.

children.name: Ovis darwini
children.description: Ovis darwini (Gobi Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis gmelini
children.description: The mouflon (Ovis gmelini) or moufflon is a wild sheep native to Cyprus, two separate parts of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Iran..

children.name: Ovis hodgsoni
children.description: Ovis hodgsoni (Tibetan Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis isphahanica
children.description: The mouflon (Ovis gmelini) or moufflon is a wild sheep native to Cyprus, two separate parts of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Iran..

children.name: Ovis jubata
children.description: Ovis jubata (Maneed Sheep) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis karelini
children.description: Ovis karelini (Karelin's Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis laristanica
children.description: The mouflon (Ovis gmelini) or moufflon is a wild sheep native to Cyprus, two separate parts of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Iran..

children.name: Ovis nigrimontana
children.description: Ovis nigrimontana (Kara-Tau Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis nivicola
children.description: The snow sheep (Ovis nivicola), or Siberian bighorn sheep, is a species of sheep from the mountainous areas in the northeast of Siberia.

children.name: Ovis polii
children.description: Ovis polii (Marco Polo Sheep) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis punjabiensis
children.description: Ovis punjabiensis (Punjab Urial) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis severtzovi
children.description: Ovis severtzovi (Severtsov's Argali) is a sheep species found in Asia region.

children.name: Ovis vignei
children.description: The urial ( OOR-ee-əl; Ovis vignei), also known as arkars, shapo, or shapu, is a wild sheep native to Central and South Asia..

children.name: Pantholops
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the chiru (Tibetan antelope), a critically threatened high-altitude antelope of the Tibetan Plateau, whose incredibly fine underfur (shahtoosh) was once heavily poached for luxury shawls.

children.name: Pantholops hodgsonii
children.description: The Tibetan antelope or chiru (Pantholops hodgsonii) ( , pronounced ; ) is a medium-sized bovid native to the northeastern Tibetan Plateau.

children.name: Pseudois
children.description: The blue sheep (bharal), two species of Himalayan caprid intermediate in appearance between sheep and goats, whose blue-grey coats make them nearly invisible against high-altitude rocky slopes and serve as a key prey species for snow leopards.

children.name: Pseudois nayaur
children.description: The bharal (Pseudois nayaur), also called the blue sheep, is a caprine native to the high Himalayas..

children.name: Pseudois schaeferi
children.description: The bharal (Pseudois nayaur), also called the blue sheep, is a caprine native to the high Himalayas..

children.name: Rupicapra
children.description: The chamois, two species of nimble mountain goat-antelopes found in the Alps, Pyrenees, Apennines, and Caucasus, celebrated for their agility on near-vertical rock faces and seasonal coat changes from tawny to dark brown.

children.name: Rupicapra asiatica
children.description: Rupicapra asiatica (Anatolian Chamois) is a chamois species found in Asia region.

children.name: Rupicapra carpatica
children.description: Rupicapra carpatica (Carpathian Chamois) is a chamois species found in Europe region.

children.name: Rupicapra ornata
children.description: Abruzzo chamois (Rupicapra pyrenaica ornata) is a goat-antelope native to the central Apennine Mountains in central and southern Italy.

children.name: Rupicapra pyrenaica
children.description: The Pyrenean chamois (Rupicapra pyrenaica) is a goat-antelope that lives in the Pyrenees and Cantabrian Mountains of Spain, France and Andorra, and the Apennine Mountains of central Italy.

children.name: Rupicapra rupicapra
children.description: The chamois (; French: [ʃamwa] ; Rupicapra rupicapra), or Alpine chamois, is a species of goat-antelope native to mountainous parts of Europe and Western Asia, from the Pyrenees and the Cantabrian Mountain Range, the Alps, the Apennines, the Dinarides, the Tatra to the Carpathian Mountains, the Balkan Mountains, the Rila–Rhodope massif, Pindus, the northeastern mountains of Turkey, and the Caucasus..
